---
title: "Minimising the largest criterion risk"
subtitle: "4.9 · after the postrank theory book, chapter 13"
description: "Comparison of weighted-risk and deterministic minimax report selection."
---

Weighted-risk selection minimises an average of expected criterion risks. Deterministic minimax selection instead
minimises their largest value. For two criteria, each report's risk line connects its criterion-specific risks;
the weighted rule selects the lowest line at the specified weight, whereas minimax selects the report with the
smallest higher endpoint. Both calculations use the same posterior law, withholding cost and feasible report family.
The examples also compare deterministic minimax risk with the maximum of the weighted lower envelope, quantities
that need not coincide in a restricted discrete family.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **w .90.** The weighted best averages .0605 but reaches .2296 when only score B counts. At **w .70**, its weighted risk is .0882 and its worse endpoint is .1378. The price panel compares each selected guarded report with the weighted best under that same loss.
- **w .30.** Both rules choose {A, B, C, D} > {E, F}; its larger expected criterion risk is .0944. The envelope peak panel distinguishes the risk value from the weight where that peak occurs.
- **Score B only.** Two weighted reports share the smallest risk. Their worst endpoint risks are .1996 and .2113; both identities, dashed alternative and complete criterion profiles remain visible.
- **Book low** and **Book high.** In the restated two-unit law, the weighted rule changes from withholding at risk .2500 to stating A above B at risk .1500. The visible table shows every eligible report's two criterion risks and their maximum.
- **Book minimax.** The guarded rule continues to withhold, with maximum .2500. Under **Zero error weight**, the same .2500 guard remains because a zero error weight does not remove a guarded criterion.
- **Certain opposition.** Exactly two grades exclude withholding. The highest point of the lower envelope is .5000, while deterministic minimax is 1.0000. This makes the gap between those two quantities visible.

::: {.callout-note}
Minimax here minimises the maximum of expected criterion risks. It does not minimise the expected maximum of realised losses. Grey full lines stay within the displayed vertical range; highlighted lines are clipped, and the keyboard and hidden table retain every eligible report. A shared grade withholds a direction rather than asserting equality. Changing the weight changes the loss, so risks at different weights are not compared as one objective.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
The package's synthetic minimax example also withholds every pair; it uses its own units.
```r
library(postrank)
source(system.file("scripts", "_vignette-setup.R", package="postrank", mustWork=TRUE), local=TRUE)
mm <- load_or_compute("toy_minimax"); get_grades(mm); get_risk(mm)
```
:::

Standalone: [worst-criterion](../../embed/worst-criterion.html), for example `?preset=high`.
